brief:
Political writer and researcher Maher Hajjazi told Shehab Wire that Palestinian activism outside the territories is widening in rejection of appointment policies and electoral blocs connected to Palestinian National Council elections. Hajjazi characterized these procedures as problematic measures that undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process.

The criticism reflects mounting Palestinian concerns over how National Council representatives are selected. Diaspora communities have begun organizing collectively against what they view as undemocratic appointment mechanisms, arguing that the system favors predetermined outcomes rather than transparent electoral procedures that would allow broader Palestinian participation in choosing their representatives.
